full_judgment:
6. On conclusion of hearing the suit, the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 20.08.1994 dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 112 of 1994 before the District Judge, Narayangonj and the learned Additional Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj hearing the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 23.03.1999 allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the defendants filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division and a learned Judge, of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.  453 of 2003 and leave was granted to consider the submission of the learned Counsel for the appellants to the following effect: 

 7. He further submits that the High Court Division has erred in affirming the decree of the court of appeal below in so far as the court of appeal below had reversed the trial courts finding about the heba-bil-ewaj deed on the ground that the executant thereof Abul Mutaleb had no independent advice while executing the same, inasmuch as this principle of law is not applicable in the case of a person like Abdul Mutaleb who was educated and was not mentally incapacitated. 

 10. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel for respondent Nos. 1, 3 and 4, on the other hand, has contended that the Appellate Court is the last Court of fact. It considered the fact that the defendants failed to examine any of the two persons who figured as witnesses in the heba deeds, particularly, Md. Shahidul Islam who took the LTI of the donor and doubted the genuineness of the heba deeds which was basically a question of fact. The High Court Division did not commit any error in law affirming the said finding of the Appellate Court. He has further contended that admittedly, the donor was a literate person, son there no reason to put his LTI instead of-putting signature and this fact also clearly corroborated the plaintiffs' case that the donor did not execute and register the heba deeds in question, the Appellate Court rightly decreed the suit and the High Court Division did not commit any error in law passing the impugned judgment and order and the same does not call for any interference by this Court and the appeal be dismissed. 

 11. From She judgment and decree of the trial Court, it appears that it did not at all consider the fact that the Contesting defendants failed to prove the execution and registration of the heba deeds in question by the donor. The trial Court also failed to consider that the defendant failed to examine the witnesses who figured in the heba deeds. The Appellate Court being last Court of fact considered the evidence on record, both oral and documentary and found that the heba deeds in question were not executed by the donor, Md. Motaleb Miah. In coming to the said finding, the Appellate Court believed exhibit- '2'on the observation that the defendant did not at all challenge the signature of Md. Motaleb Miah appearing on the exhibit and proved the same to be false. The High Court Division in affirming the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court itself considered the evidence on record. The High Court Division believed exhibit- '2' on the finding that "From the evidence of PW.5 Yusuf Hossain, the Nikah Registrar, it appears that he proved Exhibit-2, Moreover, a photocopy of the original Nikah-Nama is in the record and the signature of defendant No. 2 in that Nika-Nama is the same as that in the vokhalatnama filed with this revision application" and then gave finding that "As such, a serious doubt is created as regards the genuineness of the disputed deeds of heba-bil-ewaz." In the facts and circumstances of the case, we find nothing wrong with the Appellate Court as well as the High Court Division in relying upon exhibit- '2' in coming as to the genuineness of the heba deeds. Mr. 1 Khosnabish failed to point out any evidence on record which the Appellate Court or the High Court Division either failed to consider or misread in arriving at the finding as to the genuineness of the heba deeds in question. When the plaintiff categorically challenged that Md. Motaleb Miah was a literate person and there was no reason on his part to execute and register the heba deeds in question by putting the L.T.I., the onus was squarely upon the defendants to prove their-''genuineness by examining at least the witness who took his L.T.I in the deed.
